text:
Talia Benson: collecting notes for the lightweight retro on the compaction canary latency spike last week + what we changed after. pls drop bullets here (what happened, why, what we’re doing differently). I’ll turn into a 1-pager + action list for runtime-1.22.

Sean Gallagher: incident summary (SRE view): during Hosted canary cohort (us-east-1, ~5% traffic) we saw p99 token latency +12–18% for ~9 mins during a burst window. alert fired on p99 + scheduler lag panel. correlated strongly with kv_compaction_time_ms p99 spikes + a big jump in kv_compaction_bytes_moved/sec.

Rafael Mendes: timeline-ish (from oncall notes):
- alert at ~11:07
- triage: saw decode jitter + compaction running “hot” (steps back-to-back)
- 11:11 flipped kill-switch for cohort via rollout tool
- 11:13–11:14 metrics normalized (but config propagation lagged ~60–90s)
- kept canary paused pending fixes/guardrails

Allison Grant: metrics gap we hit: we *had* bytes moved + step counts, but not enough visibility into step time distribution at the right breakdown. the histogram was there in one place but not in the standard Hosted dash, so triage was slower than it should’ve been.

Omar El-Sayed: root cause (runtime): compaction budget was effectively bytes-driven (96MB/step in that cohort) and could execute multiple times per second because the scheduler hook was “end of decode batch” with no rate cap + no gating on backlog. under burst + mixed lengths we hit some “bad chain” relocations that took ~7–9ms for a step (copy + metadata updates), which showed up as decode stalls.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. the scheduler integration at the time didn’t have a health check. in hindsight we need “compaction is best effort” and should be skipped when:
- backlog/queue depth is high
- scheduler_lag > threshold
- we’re already missing tick targets

Julian Moore: also note: canary had tracing spans enabled for compaction exemplars (for the correlation work). helpful, but it added overhead in the hot path. not the primary cause, but it reduced headroom.

Marcus Reed: perf angle: the canary config was closer to our “Dedicated-ish” settings than Hosted. in the lab runs, 96MB/step was ok when compaction ran ~4–6/sec and step times stayed <2ms. prod churn pattern hit worst-case relocation more often, and we didn’t have a time cap so the tail of step time got ugly.

Marissa Cole: rollout / guardrails: we didn’t have an automated rollback tied to compaction metrics yet. we relied on humans + kill-switch. that worked, but it’s not acceptable as we expand cohorts.

Paula Mendes: agreed. we now have rollout policy hooks that can consume: p99 token latency delta, compaction_time p99, and scheduler_lag. we should treat it as “if compaction correlates + p99 regresses, auto-disable for cohort and freeze rollout.”

Connor O'Brien: release note for runtime-1.22 needs to call out “compaction is behind feature flag; Hosted defaults conservative; Dedicated defaults different.” also make sure the kill-switch is clearly documented + tested before it rides the train.

Samir Qureshi: changes landed / in-flight (runtime):
- compaction budget becomes min(time_cap_ms, bytes_cap) (time-first for Hosted)
- add max_steps_per_sec (hard cap)
- add cool_down_ms between steps
- add “skip_if_backlog_high / skip_if_scheduler_lag_high” gates
- make trigger earlier (avoid panic compaction)

Sean Gallagher: SRE guardrails we added post-incident:
- alert: p99 token latency + compaction_time_ms p99 together (reduce false positives)
- alert: scheduler_lag + compaction steps/sec (detect runaway)
- rollout rollback criteria: if p99 token latency +5% for 10m AND compaction_time_ms p99 > X OR scheduler_lag > Y => auto-disable + page runtime

Allison Grant: dashboard updates requested/started:
- kv_fragmentation_ratio over time (by model+tier)
- kv_compaction_time_ms histogram (p50/p95/p99) + exemplars link
- bytes moved/sec + steps/sec (rate panels)
- p99 latency overlay with compaction activity (same chart)

Rafael Mendes: runbook delta: added explicit “first 3 checks” for this failure mode:
1) is compaction enabled? what config (time_cap, bytes_cap, max_steps/sec)
2) check compaction_time_ms p99 + steps/sec
3) if p99 regresses and compaction is hot, flip kill-switch for cohort, then escalate runtime
also clarified who can flip (SRE primary + runtime secondary) and where.

Marissa Cole: comms: we should standardize the slack blast template when auto-rollback triggers (what cohort, what metrics, link to dash, link to rollout action). right now it’s ad hoc.

Paula Mendes: +1. I’ll add a template into rollout system + #eng-sre playbook.

Omar El-Sayed: learning: compaction should never be “catch up aggressively” in Hosted until we have rock-solid gating + time caps. Dedicated can tolerate more, but even there we need bounded behavior.

Marcus Reed: follow-up testing: perf-canary scenario updated to include mixed-length bursts + churn generator and enforce thresholds on:
- p99 token latency delta
- compaction_time_ms p99
- steps/sec cap respected

Talia Benson: action items (reply if I missed / wrong owner):
- [Samir] time-based cap + rate cap + cooldown fully merged behind flag; defaults set for Hosted vs Dedicated
- [Sofia/Julian] scheduler gating (backlog/lag) + metrics for skip reasons
- [Allison/Logan] standard dashboard panels + metric naming checks
- [Sean/Paula/Marissa] automated rollback policy + comms template
- [Rafael] runbook updates + config propagation validation test (ensure kill-switch applies <60s)
- [Marcus/Rina] rerun sweeps on A100/H100 and attach to canary readiness checklist
- [Connor] runtime-1.22 release train checklist includes “kill-switch tested” + “auto-rollback enabled” as gates

Sean Gallagher: looks right. one nuance: config propagation lag was ~60–90s; we should set expectation in runbook + work w/ platform on tightening. even if we can’t fix now, we need to account for it in how we interpret “recovered”.

Benji Okafor: platform side: we can shorten propagation in Hosted cohorts by adjusting cache TTL for this flag class. will coordinate w/ eng-platform thread; might not make 1.22 but we can at least reduce worst-case.

Talia Benson: perfect. keep dropping anything else here today; I’ll publish the retro notes tomorrow AM and link the updated guardrails doc + runbook.
